tool_input.description: Spot-check flag handling of refactored rotate.sh and verify.sh

result:
Done — all 9 tests pass from the repository root. (The /tmp scratch script couldn't be deleted due to sandbox permissions; it's harmless.)

What was done:
- **rotate.sh** — `surplus()` used `tail -n +"$keep"` on an oldest-first list, which deletes from the KEEP-th entry *forward*, i.e. the newest archives (with exactly N archives it deleted the newest). Now it selects the oldest `total - keep` entries (`head -n $((total - keep))`), and the "nothing to rotate" early exit fires at `total <= keep`.
- **verify.sh** — the sidecar file name was extracted with `awk '{print $2}'`, which grabs only the first word, so `my backup-….tar.gz` was truncated to `my` and reported BAD. Now the name is everything after the digest and its trailing whitespace, and the digest comparison uses a quoted `[[ ]]`.
- **lib/common.sh** — new file holding the identical option-parsing block and `resolve_dir` helper, sourced by rotate.sh and verify.sh (backup/restore/report left untouched); all flags (`--dest`, `--dest=`, `--name`, `--keep`, `-q`, `-n`, `-h`, `--`, unknown-option handling) verified to behave the same.
- **tests/run_tests.sh** — added tests: verify ok for an intact archive whose name contains spaces; rotate deletes nothing when exactly N archives exist, and deletes only the oldest when asked to keep 2 of 3.

Changed files: `rotate.sh`, `verify.sh`, `tests/run_tests.sh`, plus new `lib/common.sh`.
